question: Will the InfoGripe bulletin for epidemiological week 46 of 2026 report a national growth trend in COVID-19 SRAG hospitalisations?

calls.reasoning: Two consecutive InfoGripe editions (SE43, SE44) report a national growth signal in COVID-19 SRAG, with SARS-CoV-2 share of positives rising 8.5%->11.5% and growth spreading to six UFs. ITpS test positivity jumped from ~6.6% (end Sept) to ~17% in early Nov (highest since Feb), and mild cases are rising in 17-18 states. Hospitalisations lag positivity, so the wave is plausibly still building through SE46 (data to Nov 21). Only one horizon (6- or 3-week) needs to say growth. Risks: small counts/noise, nowcast revisions, a wording switch to estabilização/desaceleração, or growth mentioned only at state level. No market found on Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi/bookmakers.
calls.dossier:
- SE43 InfoGripe (released 2026-11-05, data to Oct 31; agencia.fiocruz.br): national growth in SRAG by metapneumovirus, rhinovirus and COVID-19; COVID growth noted in MT, DF, SP, RJ, SC (incidence very low in last four). SARS-CoV-2 = 8.5% of positives in prior 4 weeks.
- SE44 InfoGripe (released 2026-11-12, data to Nov 7; fiocruz.br news): 'sinal de crescimento do número de casos confirmados de SRAG por Covid-19' nationally; overall SRAG falling in both long and short term; SARS-CoV-2 11.5% of positives, 26.9% of positive deaths (4-wk). Growth in DF, MG, SP, RJ, PR, BA; Mato Grosso showing slowing growth. Hospitalisations described as low; no new high-intensity national wave indicated.
- UOL 2026-11-15 quotes researcher saying national severe-case trend is decreasing short and long term — this appears to refer to total SRAG, not COVID-specific (conflicting reading; Fiocruz page says COVID growth signal).
- ITpS (eshoje.com.br, Nov 2026): COVID test positivity ~17% in first week of Nov, highest since Feb 2026; +7pp in two weeks, from 6.62% end-Sept. XFG lineage ~90% of 2026 sequences.
- MS (gov.br, Nov 2026): mild COVID cases rising in 18 states; 2026 COVID SRAG burden ~3,400 hospitalisations, 437 deaths, ~63-69% below 2025. MS Informe SE43 headline: 'SRAG apresenta queda no país, apesar do aumento de alguns vírus respiratórios'.
- Status quo: latest two editions state national COVID SRAG growth.
- Base rate notes: growth signals in InfoGripe typically persist several consecutive editions once established during a rising wave; flips to 'estabilização' occur when counts plateau. Hospitalisation signal lags positivity by ~1-3 weeks. Not found: a counted historical persistence rate.
- Resolution instrument: resolves off national text (Pontos de destaque / Situação nacional) of Resumo InfoGripe SE46 2026, not state-level or death-only statements; either 6- or 3-week growth suffices.
- Event window: single bulletin SE46 (data through Nov 21, publication expected Nov 26); as of 2026-11-16 the SE46 week is ~15% elapsed; SE45 edition (expected ~Nov 19) not yet out.
- Searched but not found: SE45 bulletin; any prediction market (none on Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi/bookmakers); text of SE44 PDF itself (could not extract).
calls.reference_class: InfoGripe virus-specific national growth signals: persistence of a 'sinal de crescimento' 2 editions after it appears during an early-stage wave

calls.reasoning: InfoGripe reported national COVID-19 SRAG growth in SE 43 and SE 44, and growth is spreading geographically (SE43: MT, DF, SP, RJ, SC; SE44: DF, MG, SP, RJ, PR, BA), with the Ministry of Health reporting mild cases rising in 18-19 states. This looks like the early phase of a second-half wave led by populous Centre-South states, and InfoGripe growth signals early in a wave usually persist for several editions; SE 46 is only two editions after SE 44. Risks: small national counts, nowcast noise, and early deceleration (Mato Grosso already shows 'desaceleração'), any of which could lead the bulletin to describe the national trend as stabilising or decelerating. No human prediction market found (harness Polymarket/Manifold search found none; my own searches found none; Kalshi and bookmakers not checked directly).
calls.dossier:
- SE 44 InfoGripe (released 12 Nov 2026; data through 7 Nov): national SRAG overall shows a falling signal in both long-term (6 wk) and short-term (3 wk) trends; national COVID-19 SRAG and metapneumovirus SRAG show a growth signal (question background; Fiocruz news page 12 Nov). Fiocruz news headline: 'InfoGripe aponta aumento do número de casos de Covid-19'.
- SE 44: states with COVID SRAG growth were DF, MG, SP, RJ, PR (Centre-South) and BA (Northeast). Mato Grosso already shows 'sinal de desaceleração do crescimento' of COVID SRAG (fiocruz.br, 12 Nov 2026).
- SE 43 (released 5 Nov; data through 31 Oct): national growth in SRAG from metapneumovirus, rhinovirus and COVID-19; states with COVID increases were MT, DF, SP, RJ, SC, with SP/RJ/SC at 'muito baixos' levels (agorarn.com.br). The Ministry of Health listed 19 states with upward COVID trends as of 5 Nov.
- From SE 43 to SE 44 the set of states with growth shifted and widened (MG, PR and BA added; MT decelerating).
- SARS-CoV-2 accounted for 11.5% of positive SRAG cases over the last 4 weeks vs 4.0% year-to-date, and 26.9% of positive SRAG deaths (SE 44).
- Absolute COVID levels are low; the researcher (Tatiana Portella) said the situation is 'not yet worrying' (O Globo, 14 Nov). The 2026 COVID burden is about 63% below 2025 (Ministry of Health).
- Caution: a UOL article (15 Nov) says 'the national trend for severe cases is decreasing' — this most likely refers to all-cause SRAG, not COVID-specific SRAG.
- Ministry of Health / ITpS: rising flu-like illness cases and COVID test positivity over the last 6 weeks, consistent with previous second-half waves (O Globo, 14 Nov).
- Status quo: national COVID SRAG described as growing for 2 consecutive editions (SE 43, SE 44).
- Resolution instrument: resolves off the national-level text (highlights / Situação nacional) of the SE 46 Resumo, expected 26 Nov; state-level growth statements do not count.
- Event window: one bulletin (SE 46, data through 21 Nov), published ~26 Nov; as of 16 Nov the SE 45 bulletin (due ~19 Nov) is not yet out.
- Searched for but not found: the SE 45 bulletin, readable SE 44 PDF text (extraction failed), and any prediction market (none).
calls.reference_class: InfoGripe national virus-specific growth signals in the early phase of a wave (2 consecutive editions), persisting 2 more editions

calls.reasoning: National COVID-19 SRAG growth signal reported in three consecutive InfoGripe editions (SE42 'leve crescimento... em nível nacional', SE43, SE44), with growth spreading to six states (DF, MG, SP, RJ, PR, BA) and SARS-CoV-2 share of positives rising to 11.5% (4-week) vs 4.0% YTD. InfoGripe growth signals typically persist several editions, and the 6-week long-term trend lags, so either horizon showing growth at SE46 is more likely than not. Risks: small national counts, nowcast revisions, Mato Grosso already decelerating, overall SRAG falling; flip to 'estabilização' within two weeks is plausible. No human market found (harness found none on Polymarket/Manifold; no Kalshi/bookmaker contract plausible).

calls.reference_class: InfoGripe national virus-specific growth signals that have persisted 3 consecutive editions: fraction still reporting growth 2 editions later

calls.reasoning: InfoGripe has reported national COVID-19 SRAG growth in at least two consecutive editions (SE43, SE44), likely three (SE42 'leve crescimento... em nível nacional'). Leading indicators are still rising: ITpS positivity ~6.6% end-Sept to ~17% early Nov, the SARS-CoV-2 share of positives 8.5% to 11.5%, and the set of growing states widening into the populous Centre-South. Hospitalisations lag positivity, and the 6-week trend lags further; either horizon showing growth suffices. Risks: small national counts, nowcast noise, early deceleration (MT), and wording switching to estabilização/desaceleração within two editions. No human market found.
calls.reconciliation: Factual disputes: (1) whether SE42 already reported national COVID growth. Only Run 3 cites it (bvs.br), and it is consistent with the trajectory, so I accept it as likely. Either way, growth is confirmed for two editions. (2) The UOL 15 Nov 'decreasing severe-case trend' quote. All three runs read it as all-cause SRAG, consistent with SE44 overall SRAG falling while the Fiocruz SE44 page explicitly states COVID growth. Not a contradiction. (3) Run 1's positivity data (ITpS ~17%) is uncontested and supports a still-building wave. The remaining disagreement is judgment about persistence over two editions. Rising leading indicators and the lagging 6-week horizon favour persistence; the small counts and MT deceleration are real but secondary. I take ~0.78. No retrieval this run.
